title: DERMA-GUARD: Evidence-Aware Specialist Consensus with Risk-Controlled Evidence Acquisition and Deferral for Multimodal Dermatology
name: Rachit Agarwal
keywords: multimodal dermatology, evidential deep learning, Dempster-Shafer fusion, learned evidence gating, conformal prediction, Learn-then-Test, selective prediction, evidence acquisition, clinical decision support

abstract: Skin-lesion AI has reached dermatologist-level accuracy on curated images, and apps that classify a photographed mole are already in public use. Almost all of them share a dangerous habit: they always answer. A blurred photograph, missing history, or a photograph and history that disagree still produce a confident label, and the confidence shown is rarely calibrated. In dermatology the costliest error of all is a cancer that is confidently called harmless.

DERMA-GUARD is a decision-support system that behaves more like a careful clinician. Building on two base papers, HOT AI and Learn-then-Test, and on the paired MILK10k dataset, it combines six specialists (evidential heads for the photograph, dermoscopy and patient details, our earlier prototype's image model, a similar-case vote and a class-balanced embedding classifier). A Devil's Advocate profiles every specialist on every case, and a learned gate, chosen from seven combination rules under cross-fitting, decides how much each opinion counts. A calibrated, cost-aware policy then gives a high-confidence answer, a clearly marked low-confidence answer for a doctor to confirm, a request for more evidence (dermoscopy, missing details or a better photograph), or a referral when the evidence contradicts itself, with the missed-cancer rate certified by Learn-then-Test.

On 787 held-out MILK10k lesions, the system answers 89.1% of patients; 57.1% receive a high-confidence answer that is 77.1% accurate across eleven diagnoses and misses 3.1% of cancers, against 4.9% for a learned rejector at the same coverage (p = 0.011). Learned fusion raises photograph-only macro-F1 from 0.286 to 0.377. Across four fusion back-ends the policy's miss rate stays between 3.0% and 3.5%, while a confidence threshold ranges from 3.5% to 9.3%. Evidential uncertainty alone misses blurred, dark, noisy and occluded photographs; explicit checks remove every confident answer on damaged input. On PAD-UFES-20 and Derm7pt, without retraining, the safety target holds while fine-grained diagnosis does not transfer.
